title: Lesson 25: Engagement Models and Pricing: Fixed-Fee vs Hourly vs Retainer, and When Each Fits
description: Choosing the engagement model (fixed-fee, hourly, or retainer) that matches the delivery style and risk of consulting work, and how the choice decides who carries the risk of being wrong about scope.

questions.question: Per the lesson on engagement models, what is the real decision behind choosing a pricing model?
options: Which model lets you bill the highest hourly rate
Which model produces a fixed monthly income
Who bears the risk of scope, and who the engagement model matches that risk to
Which model requires the least paperwork to invoice
questions.explanation: The lesson frames the engagement model as the contract over who bears the risk of being wrong about scope, and that risk split is where the money and trust live, not the rate itself.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the lesson's guidance on when each model fits?
options: Fixed-fee fits work whose scope you have done before and define tightly
Retainer is best for a one-shot implementation
Hourly fits work where the outcome is already clearly defined
Any model works equally for exploration, known outcomes, and ongoing operations
questions.explanation: The lesson teaches fixed-fee where the outcome is well defined and familiar, hourly where scope is genuinely uncertain, and retainer where there is ongoing operational need.

questions.question: Which conclusion does the lesson support about a retainer?
options: A retainer is a discount on a bulk block of hours
A retainer should name the set of included work, not just the hours it might cover
A retainer is only for the initial implementation phase
Under a retainer, your incentive is to bill for fighting incidents rather than preventing them
questions.explanation: The lesson warns that a retainer priced as hours in bulk is really hourly, and that a real retainer names the included work. It also teaches the retainer incentive is to prevent incidents so the system stays boring and the relationship renews.
